Between N_b3 and B would be R4 =? B to N_b3 measured 20. So R4 =20. Then total A-B = sum =11.667+10+15+20 =56.667 matches measurement! Good. So chain fits.

Now X1 connections: measurements: A-X1 =6.667, B-X1=50, N_b1-X1=5, N_b2-X1=15, N_b3-X1=30. In a simple chain, X1 could be a node connected to some point via a resistor to ground? If X1 is connected to each node via separate resistors, then the measured resistance between X1 and a node would be the parallel combination of the direct resistor and paths through other resistors to other nodes then back via their resistors. But maybe X1 is simply a node attached to the chain at a point between A and N_b1 via resistor 6.667, and also to N_b1 via 5, etc. Could be that X1 is a node that is connected to the chain at a single point (like a tap) but the measurements reflect series resistances.
